stemBlocks.value: Make x the subject of the formula y = 7x.
Think first: Here x is multiplied by 7, so division is the operation that frees it.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p055-q03 from workbook page 55.

solutionSteps.instruction: Identify what is being done to x.

whyThisWorks.value: Multiplication and division are inverse operations, so dividing both sides by 7 cancels the 7 attached to x while keeping the two sides equal. The result x = y/7 says that x is one seventh of y, which is the same relationship read the other way round. No number can be found for x because y is itself a variable.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing x = y − 7 by subtracting instead of dividing.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing x = y − 7 by subtracting instead of dividing.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing x = 7y by multiplying rather than dividing.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing x = 7y by multiplying rather than dividing.

commonErrors.misconception: Dividing only one side of the formula by 7.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Dividing only one side of the formula by 7.

examTip.value: Match the inverse to the operation: addition pairs with subtraction, multiplication with division. Choosing the wrong pair is the single most common error in this topic.
